classification.difficultyReason: Complete the supplied value table and translate each row into a smooth curve on the given axes. The essential distinction is between negating the output and negating the exponent, using the taught reflection and negative-index methods.

inlines.text: Plot these graphs on the same axis.

spec.description: Blank tall coordinate grid with square unit cells, double-ended axes, every nonzero integer labelled, and no origin label or response curves.
spec.mathematics: x ranges from -4 to 4; y ranges from -10 to 10; grid and ticks have step 1.
spec.answerVisibility: Student scaffold only; completed curves are in the answer figure.

inlines.text: . Plot each row and join with smooth curves. Negating y reflects in the x-axis; replacing x by −x reflects in the y-axis.

spec.description: Complete solution graph on the supplied unit grid, with all 21 table points and three smooth curves. A two-row legend and distinct strokes identify the curves.
spec.mathematics: Plots y=2^x, y=-(2^x), and y=2^{-x} on -4≤x≤4 and -10≤y≤10. Intercepts are (0,1), (0,-1), and (0,1); horizontal asymptote is y=0.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer only; used for both short answers and worked solutions.
